newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via eight-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via eight-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Wednesday via eight-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"We see the Fed adding through eight-day system RPs," said Lee Youngdahl, vice-president at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co Inc.
An economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc agreed, saying he as well expects the Fed to add reserves through an eight-day system operation.
Some economists, however, expect the Fed to remain out of the market ahead of the outcome of Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
Analysts at Dean Witter Reynolds and consulting firm MMS International said the Fed will likely refrain from adding reserves to the banking system.
At 1100 EST/1600 GMT, the federal funds rate was quoted at 5-1/4 percent, in line with the central bank's target.
